To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a practical, standard-compliant rate adaptation (RA), closed-loop solution for MIMO 802.n networks.
we propose a practical metric that accurately captures 802.11 n link quality and a standard-compliant RA solution that jointly selects rate and channel width.

we propose diffSNR, a practical and deployable metric for measuring link quality in 802.1n MIMO networks, and we use diffSNR to build performance models that predict link quality with 95.5 percent accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the performance of 802.11 wireless LANs, and our proposed solution, ARAMIS with its link metric diffSNR, can help achieve this goal.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work provides a practical framework for 80.11 MIMO RA that accurately captures channel quality and adapts transmission settings on a per-paket basis.
we present a new link metric that accurately models 802.11 n performance and a new rate adaptation algorithm that uses the new link metric to improve throughput in 802.1n networks.

ARAMIS is the first rate adaptation algorithm that is able to adapt to a wide range of 802.11 environments with negligible overhead, while providing a significant performance boost in 802.1n environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ARAMIS is the first practical, deployable, closed-loop, 801.11n RA algorithm that accurately adapts rate and MIMO transmission technique to channel conditions with minimal overhead.
ARAMIS is the first RA solution that can simultaneously adapt rate and bandwidth in MIMO 11n environments.
we provide a practical framework for MIMO RA that can be used to build efficient, standard-compliant, and deployable solutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diffSNR and ARAMIS provide a practical framework that can accurately capture and exploit the benefits of MIMO 802.n networks.
ARAMIS is a simple yet practical solution for rate adaptation in 802.1n environments.
a practical link metric, diffSNR, and an efficient closed-loop RA framework, ARAMIS, are key to maximizing the performance of 802.11 wireless networks.
